title: NBK Profit Rises 61% to KSh1.72 Billion in First Half
desc: National Bank of Kenya posted a 61% rise in first-half profit as lending grew and loan loss provisions fell sharply.
content:
National Bank of Kenya has recorded a strong first-half performance, with profit after tax rising by 61% to KSh1.72 billion for the six months ending June 30, 2026.

The lender posted a profit of KSh1.07 billion during the same period last year, meaning its latest results represent a significant improvement in earnings.

The growth was supported by stronger net interest income, improved credit quality and continued cost management.

One of the biggest changes in the bank's performance was a sharp fall in loan loss provisions. These declined to KSh80.9 million from about KSh1 billion in the first half of 2025, reflecting improved recoveries and credit quality.

NBK's net interest income also increased by 11% to KSh5.40 billion, up from KSh4.87 billion a year earlier.

The bank also recorded growth across key areas of its balance sheet.

Total assets increased to about KSh157 billion from KSh141 billion at the end of December 2025. Customer deposits rose to KSh116.3 billion, while net loans and advances grew to about KSh61 billion.

The figures point to continued expansion in lending and deposits as the bank pursues its transformation strategy under parent company Access Bank.

For customers and businesses, growth in lending can signal an increased ability by banks to support households and companies seeking financing.

However, the strong profit growth was not driven by lending alone. The major reduction in credit impairment charges also played an important role in improving the bank's bottom line.

NBK said it remains focused on strengthening customer experience, expanding its digital capabilities, maintaining disciplined risk management and improving operational efficiency.

The first-half performance gives the lender a stronger financial position as it continues its transformation journey.

Attention will now turn to whether NBK can maintain the momentum during the second half of the year as Kenya's banking sector continues to operate in a competitive economic environment.
